# Appeal of Denial — Lower Back Disc Surgery / Decompression (CPT 63030)

**RE: Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-07**
**Member: Jordan Foster**
**Member ID: W794852405**
**Reference number: POC-EE22487639-86426**
**Plan: Ambetter (WellCare), Commercial/ACA, North Carolina**
**Governing policy: Clinical Policy: Disc Decompression Procedures (CP.MP.114)** — https://www.ambetterhealth.com/content/dam/centene/ambetteril/clinical-policies/CP.MP.114.pdf

Dear Ambetter (WellCare) Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for lower back disc surgery (CPT 63030), which my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, has documented is medically necessary. I am asking the plan to reconsider this decision.

## Why I believe the denial should be reversed

The denial states that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I do not believe this is accurate, and I would like the plan to look again at what is already in my file against its own published criteria.

The plan's policy, CP.MP.114, states that discectomy is medically necessary when meeting all of the following, including:

> "Ne rve root compression confirmed by imaging and one of the following:"

My MRI from 2026-06-28 shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. This is documented nerve root compression confirmed by imaging.

The policy also requires:

> "Radiculopathy with sensory deficit as evidenced by pain, parasthesias or numbness in a nerve root distribution, and member/enrollee has failed to respond to conservative ther apy including all the following:"

My records document radicular pain extending into my right calf, positive provocative testing on the affected side, and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes at a time because of this pain.

As for the conservative care itself, the policy states:

> "Member/enrollee has failed to respond to conservative therapy, within the last year, including all of the following:"

and specifically:

> "a) ≥ four wee ks physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program, or documentation of member/enrollee’s inability to tolerate;"

I completed 16 visits of supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, over 10 weeks from 2026-05-03 to 2026-07-12. This is documented in my physical therapy discharge note and is well beyond the four-week minimum in the policy.

The policy also requires:

> "1) Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) or acetaminophen ≥ thre e weeks unless contraindicated or not tolerated;"

and

> "2) Epidural steroid inj ection;"

I took NSAIDs for approximately 6 months with inadequate relief, well beyond the three-week minimum, and I received an epidural steroid injection on 2026-06-09, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief before my symptoms returned.

Taken together, my records show 12 months of progressive low back pain unrelieved by rest, more than 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy, more than 6 months of NSAID use, and an epidural steroid injection with only temporary benefit — all within the past year, as the policy requires. My MRI confirms nerve root compression, and my exam findings and symptoms document radiculopathy with sensory deficit in the affected nerve root distribution.

[If my chart also documents ≥ four weeks of activity modification, as referenced in the policy, I ask that this be confirmed from the record and counted toward this criterion.]

Given this, I do not believe the stated reason for denial — an inadequate trial of conservative treatment — is consistent with what is already documented in my file and with the plan's own policy.

## What I am requesting

I am asking the plan to reconsider this denial and to approve the requested surgery based on the records already submitted, or to let me know promptly what additional documentation is needed to complete the review.

## Deadline and how I am submitting this appeal

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-03. I am submitting it through the appeal process described on my denial notice, and/or through ambetterhealth.com by selecting North Carolina and using that state's appeal or grievance form, and by calling the number on my member ID card if I need to confirm submission.

Thank you for reconsidering my request.

Sincerely,

Jordan Foster
Member ID: W794852405
[Date]
[Contact phone number]
[Contact address]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
